rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Air pollution — causes, effects, and control ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Air pollution — causes** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Environmental Issues fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Air pollution is the addition of harmful substances to the atmosphere — gases (CO, SO2, NOx), particulates (PM2.5, PM10) and secondary products (photochemical smog, acid rain). Sources are combustion, industry and vehicles; effects range from respiratory disease to acid rain and global climate change. Control combines technology (filters, converters), fuel policy and law.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Pollutant table: CO (haemoglobin affinity → death), SO2/NOx (acid rain), particulates (respiratory disease), CFCs (ozone), lead (nervous system) — one effect each.  ·  Trick 2: Acid rain chemistry: SO2 + OH → H2SO4; NOx → HNO3, pH < 5.6 — the two acid names earn the mark.

Worked examples and applications ≥ 6 worked examples with solved steps, live examples and Nepal-context applications (biology-plan.md §3.1, block V) — written in the unit fill pass. ## 6. Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — why lead killed catalytic converters.** A catalytic converter uses platinum-group catalysts to finish the combustion of CO and NOx. Lead in old petrol coats the catalyst surface in weeks and destroys it — which is why unleaded petrol was a precondition for converter-based emission norms everywhere.…  ·  ## 7.
